name: Baltic Threshold
summary: A fictional border crisis near allied territory creates fears of wider conventional escalation.
background: A disputed military exercise near a fictional Baltic corridor leads to air and cyber incidents. All sides issue public statements, but private signals are contradictory.
initial_state: Forward units are on alert, civilian evacuation rumors spread online, and a hotline exchange is delayed by translation disputes.

United States.political_objective: Assure allies and deter coercion without transforming the crisis into a strategic confrontation.
United States.military_position: Conventional reinforcements are available but vulnerable to misinterpretation.

Russia.political_objective: Demonstrate resolve and prevent perceived encirclement while preserving bargaining leverage.
Russia.military_position: Regional forces are postured for rapid signaling but logistics are strained.

NATO.political_objective: Maintain alliance cohesion and avoid uncontrolled escalation.
NATO.military_position: Defensive posture is visible but politically contested.

China.political_objective: Avoid uncontrolled great-power escalation while extracting diplomatic advantage from allied distraction.
China.military_position: No direct theater role, but strategic forces monitor changes in global alert levels.
